subject: Ephemeral headroom definitions & autoscale throttles for ApexAI Dedicated
messages:
From: Lina Ortega <lina.ortega@apexai.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@apexai.com
Date: 2027-05-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify ephemeral headroom for Dedicated commitment

Hi Connor,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As we finalize the SOW, procurement asked for clearer definitions around the ephemeral/burst headroom — specifically how Redwood will meter and enforce burst caps against our reserved slab and what preemption/eviction behavior looks like during peak windows.

Two concrete asks from our side:
- A clear headroom matrix (percent of reserved capacity that can be used as soft burst vs hard burst, by time-of-day).
- The autoscale throttle and eviction policy details (notification windows, grace period, how preemptible workloads are reclaimed).

Can you share a short proposal so we can attach it to the contract addendum? We need this for legal/procurement to sign off.

Thanks,
Lina Ortega
Head of Platform Engineering
ApexAI

[Attachment: requirements-apex-20270517.pdf]

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Ortega <lina.ortega@apexai.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-18T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify ephemeral headroom for Dedicated commitment

Hi Lina —

Appreciate the clear asks. Attached is a compact headroom matrix and a proposal for autoscale throttles that we think will meet ApexAI's availability goals while keeping unit economics reasonable. High-level summary:

- Soft-burst (preferred): up to 30% additional vGPU capacity over reserved slab during Business Hours (08:00-20:00 local) with automated smoothing. Soft-burst is credit-backed and we absorb up to 15% immediate shortfall; beyond that, bursts consume credits or trigger preemption based on policy.
- Hard-burst (guaranteed, contract-bound): up to 10% additional capacity available for short-lived spikes with explicit credit consumption and 1-minute eviction notice for preemptible jobs.

Autoscale throttles (default proposal):
- scale_window_seconds: 30s
- max_continuous_burst_minutes: 20
- eviction_grace_seconds: 300 (5 minutes)
- preemptible_label: "soft-burst" (we mark and reclaim KV caches first)

Attached file: Apex_Dedicated_Burst_Matrix_v3.xlsx — contains the hourly matrix and cost multipliers.

Next steps: if this aligns with Apex's needs, we can codify it into an SLA addendum and provide a short runbook for your SREs. Monica, Karthik — can you add ops and commercial notes respectively?

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: Apex_Dedicated_Burst_Matrix_v3.xlsx]

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>, Lina Ortega <lina.ortega@apexai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-18T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify ephemeral headroom for Dedicated commitment

Thanks Connor and Lina — adding ops perspective. I reviewed the matrix and propose the following operational guardrails (keeps tenant isolation tight while providing predictable burst behavior):

- Definitions:
  - Baseline: reserved slab (committed GPUs).
  - Soft-headroom: ephemeral buffer used to smooth short queues; reclaimed without SLA credit if within defined smoothing window.
  - Hard-headroom: explicit contracted burst that counts against credits and has explicit preemption policy.

- Suggested numbers (ops defaults we will ship unless Apex requests otherwise):
  - Business Hours (08:00-20:00): soft-headroom = 25% of reserved, hard-headroom = 10%
  - Off-hours (20:00-08:00): soft-headroom = 15%, hard-headroom = 10%
  - Peak-week (scheduled launches): allow temporary soft-headroom +10% for up to 4 hours with 24h notice from customer.

- Autoscale behavior:
  - scale_window_seconds = 30 (same as Connor)
  - smoothing: moving-average across 3 windows to avoid flapping
  - eviction policy: notify tenant 300s, mark preemptible tasks and begin graceful KV checkpointing; if tasks are not reclaimable within 300s, force preempt.

- Observability: we will expose a /metrics endpoint per tenant showing burst usage, reclaim events, and headroom credits consumed.

Attached is a short ops runbook snippet for your SREs. We can expand into a runbook PDF for the contract.

Monica Patel
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: dedicated-autoscale-runbook.md]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Ortega <lina.ortega@apexai.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-18T12:55:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify ephemeral headroom for Dedicated commitment

Lina — quick commercial notes so procurement has what it needs:

- Credits & metering: soft-burst will be metered at 0.6x on-demand multiplier (discounted), hard-burst at 1.2x (premium); we credit back unused soft-headroom if monthly consumption is below committed expectation.
- Contract language: propose an addendum with two items — 1) hourly headroom matrix (ops-specified) and 2) crediting rules (monthly reconciliation).
- Escalation & governance: include a 72-hour review SLA for disputed reclaim events. We can add an internal JIRA webhook to sync reclaim events for audits.

Deal ID: DEAL-2027-1138
I will draft the short addendum and link the DocuSign envelope once Lina confirms the matrix.

Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

Connor O'Brien
